an4.67:1.1: At one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
an4.67:1.2: Then at that time near Sāvatthī a certain monk was bitten by a snake and died.
an4.67:1.3: Then a great many monks approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side. While sitting on one side those monks said this to the Fortunate One:
an4.67:1.4: “Here, reverend Sir, near Sāvatthī, a certain monk has been bitten by a snake and has died”.
an4.67:2.1: “Surely, monks, that monk did not suffuse the four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness.
an4.67:2.2: For if, monks, that monk had suffused the four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness then that monk, monks, would not have been bitten by a snake and died.
an4.67:3.1: Who are the four royal families of snakes?
an4.67:3.2: The Virūpakkha royal family of snakes, the Erāpatha royal family of snakes, the Chabyāputta royal family of snakes, the Kaṇhāgotamaka royal family of snakes.
an4.67:3.3: Surely, monks, that monk did not suffuse these four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness.
an4.67:3.4: For if, monks, that monk had suffused these four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness, then that monk, monks, would not have been bitten by a snake and died.
an4.67:4.1: I allow you, monks, to suffuse these four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness, to guard yourselves, to protect yourselves, to safeguard yourselves.”
an4.67:5.1: I am friendly with the Virūpakkhas,
an4.67:5.2: with the Erāpathas I am friendly,
an4.67:5.3: I am friendly with the Chabyāputtas,
an4.67:6.1: I am friendly with those without feet,
an4.67:6.2: with those with two feet I am friendly,
an4.67:6.3: I am friendly with those with four feet,
an4.67:6.4: with those with many feet I am friendly.
an4.67:7.1: May the one without feet not hurt me,
an4.67:7.2: may the one with two feet not hurt me,
an4.67:7.3: may the one with four feet not hurt me,
an4.67:7.4: may the one with many feet not hurt me.
an4.67:8.1: May all beings, all living creatures,
an4.67:8.2: all who are born, in their entirety,
an4.67:8.4: may nothing bad come to anyone.
an4.67:10.3: I have made this protection, I have made this safeguard,
an4.67:10.6: I revere the seven Perfect Sambuddhas.”
